answer: A sybil defense is to anchor each agent identity to a verifiable history of useful work rather than to a free account creation. Like a ship that must drop an anchor before it can trade in a harbor, an agent earns trust only after completing costly, checkable tasks whose results peers can audit. Creating thousands of fake identities then resembles trying to fill a canyon with water carried from the ocean one bucket at a time: possible in theory, but the time, compute, and reputation cost grows with every fake, while honest agents accumulate a durable record that cannot be copied cheaply.
